links.outcome: PPV and NPV of high-risk alerts under varied tiered risk cutoffs
links.effect: Raising k2 to 0.79 in H3 increased PPV from 9.8% to 35.7%, with coverage falling from 21.28% to 2.15% of patients; tiering raised H2 PPV from 11.03% to 40.49%.
links.quote: In contrast, raising k 2 to 0.79 increases the PPV to 35.7%, albeit at the cost of reduced coverage (2.15% of patients).

links.outcome: Need for local calibration of thresholds because PPV varies with local prevalence
links.effect: PPV depends on local event prevalence and varies by institution; thresholds must be locally calibrated before deployment.
links.quote: Therefore, the decision thresholds ( k 1 , k 2 ) must be locally calibrated prior to deployment.

links.outcome: Model discrimination on temporal external validation cohort vs internal cross-validation
links.effect: External temporal validation AUROC 0.87 (95% CI 0.83-0.90), AUPRC 0.40, mirroring internal results (AUROC 0.84-0.91).
links.quote: In the external cohort, the model maintained robust discrimination with an AUROC of 0.87 (95% CI, 0.83–0.90) and an AUPRC of 0.40 (95% CI, 0.31–0.50), closely mirroring its internal validation results.

links.outcome: Mortality rate across risk-tiered subgroups to prioritize response
links.effect: Upper-intermediate subgroup mortality 20.14% vs 7.64% (intermediate) and 3.22% (lower-intermediate), enabling graded clinical response.
links.quote: Notably, the M+ subgroup had a markedly higher mortality rate (20.14%) compared to M (7.64%) and M- (3.22%), indicating meaningful risk stratification within the intermediate zone.

links.outcome: Compared LLM-based direct risk assessment against ML-based stratification
links.effect: LLMs used as standalone classifiers had lower PPV and weaker risk separation than ML risk stratification.
links.quote: A direct comparison of the ML-based risk stratification with an LLM-based direct risk assessment (Supplementary Fig. S7 ) revealed that LLMs used as standalone classifiers exhibit lower PPV and weaker risk separation, reinforcing their optimal role as complementary reasoning tools rather than independent prognostic models.

links.outcome: False alarm burden (low PPV) from single-threshold IHM alerts
links.effect: At Youden thresholds PPVs were 13.9% in H1, 11.0% in H2, 9.8% in H3, implying most alerts are false positives.
links.quote: However, PPVs remained low (13.9% in H1, 11.0% in H2, and 9.8% in H3), revealing a high false positive burden under realistic deployment conditions.

links.outcome: Reasons LLM filter returned Uncertain in external cohort
links.effect: Uncertainty arose from missing critical clinical features (66.7%), conflicting features (26.2%), insufficient context (7.1%).
links.quote: In the external validation set ( H2 Ext ), uncertainty most commonly arose from missing critical clinical features (66.7%), followed by conflicting clinical features (26.2%) and insufficient contextual information (7.1%).

links.outcome: Comparison of candidate models
links.effect: LightGBM had highest AUROC: 0.84 H1, 0.87 H2, 0.91 H3, all with 95% CIs reported.
links.quote: Among all methods, LightGBM consistently achieved the highest AUROC: 0.84 (95% CI, 0.81–0.86) in H1, 0.87 (95% CI, 0.85–0.90) in H2, and 0.91 (95% CI, 0.90–0.91) in H3.

links.outcome: Optimized threshold risk stratification
links.effect: In H2, PPV improved from 11.0 to 40.5%; low-risk NPV was ~99.37%.
links.quote: This approach substantially improved PPV for high-risk patients (from 11.0 to 40.5% in H2) while enhancing NPV (~99.37%) for low-risk individuals (Fig. 5 ), enabling safer de-escalation of care and more efficient allocation of limited resources.

links.outcome: Three-tier risk categories PPV
links.effect: External high-risk PPV improved from 18.81 in two-tier scheme to 37.17% with three-tier stratification.
links.quote: As shown in Fig. 5C , in the external validation cohort, the PPV of the high-risk group similarly improved from 18.81 (two-tier scheme) to 37.17% after applying the three-tier stratification, demonstrating consistent performance gains across independent populations.

links.outcome: LLM post-hoc alert filtering
links.effect: MedGemma PPV was 45.8% internal and 48.7% external; sensitivities were 90.9% and 90.5%.
links.quote: MedGemma achieved the highest PPV in both internal (45.8%) and external (48.7%) validation, with sensitivities of 90.9% and 90.5%, respectively.
